title: Slow-cooker turkey chilli
subtitle: A leaner chilli, as good as the beef version
excerpt: Turkey mince with kidney beans, tinned tomatoes, and a full spice base. Lighter than a beef chilli but just as hearty and satisfying.
sourceNotes: Turkey chilli is a widely made American home-cooking dish, popularised as a leaner alternative to beef chilli. The method draws on standard American chilli con carne recipes adapted for turkey mince.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat on the hob.
recipe.batchNotes: An excellent batch-cook recipe. The flavour only improves over two to three days in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. The spices settle and deepen overnight.

content.text: Turkey mince makes a very good chilli. It takes on spice well, stays moist in the slow cooker, and produces a result that is noticeably lighter than a beef version without tasting thin. The beans provide the texture and body that the leaner mince cannot supply on its own.

You can add the mince raw to the slow cooker, though browning it first in a hot pan for 5 minutes gives the finished chilli a better colour and a deeper flavour. Either approach works; choose based on how much time you have.
Serve with rice, baked potatoes, or cornbread. Soured cream and grated cheese are good alongside.

Heat a dry frying pan over high heat. Add {{turkey-mince}} of turkey mince and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until no longer pink and beginning to colour. Transfer to the slow cooker.

Add the drained {{kidney-beans}} of kidney beans, {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree, {{onion}} diced onion, {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, and {{pepper-red}} diced red pepper to the slow cooker. Add {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, and {{coriander-ground}} of coriander. Pour in {{stock-chicken}} of chicken stock and season with {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Stir to combine.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 6 to 8 hours, stirring once or twice if possible. The chilli is ready when the sauce is thick and deep red. Squeeze in lime juice, taste, and adjust seasoning before serving.

rows.symptom: The turkey mince clumped together in the slow cooker
rows.cause: Turkey mince added raw tends to clump into large pieces without the benefit of breaking apart in a hot pan.
rows.fix: Stir vigorously with a spoon to break up the clumps. Next time, brown the mince in a pan first, which naturally breaks it into smaller pieces.

rows.cause: The tinned tomatoes and stock added more liquid than the beans could absorb during cooking.
rows.fix: Set to HIGH with the lid off for 30 minutes to reduce. Or stir through a spoonful of tomato puree and let it cook for 10 more minutes.

rows.symptom: The flavour tastes raw and spicy rather than rounded
rows.cause: The spices were not bloomed in oil before adding, which leaves them with a slightly sharp edge.
rows.fix: Add a small pinch of sugar and a squeeze of lime juice to round the flavour. Next time, fry the spices briefly in a pan before adding to the slow cooker.

rows.symptom: The turkey is dry and grainy
rows.cause: Turkey mince can become very dry if it is extra-lean and cooked too long on HIGH.
rows.fix: Use LOW setting only for turkey, and aim for 6 rather than 8 hours. Stir in a splash of chicken stock if the texture feels too dry.

content.text: Turkey chilli came into British kitchens alongside the wider adoption of turkey as a year-round protein rather than just a Christmas centrepiece. It sits in the same category as chicken mince dishes: lighter than beef, more affordable than lamb, and very well suited to the slow cooker. It is one of the better uses for turkey mince outside of December.
